text:
When I hear the glitter of the empty bells vibrate I realize

that Napoleon had toes

Frankenstein a big toe

Hayagriva, cosmic horse, a split big toe

The Virgin Mary, white feet, married Joseph, brown feet; a transparent white dove inseminated her

with three toes


How many toes does God have? No one knows Yahweh’s feet

or Allah’s? Muhammad, prophetic ten

Jesus Christ certainly kissed human toes


Sealo, the Seal Boy, who had flipper-hands on his shoulders

with two fingers could smoke and type with all ten toes

he sold little white deodorizers wrapped in toilet paper, one-dollar souvenirs


Shelley, ten pure pale fingers

Michelangelo had five digits per foot, Da Vinci drew ten across his two feet


The flies’ toes remain stuck to spiderwebs

spiders slide their swift feet along sticky webs

they sting the soles, the toes curl


One dark Friday night I struck the fourth toe of my bare foot against the little stair

but it still moves

walking through mud with snow is hard, it hurts the back


John Madison has chocolate toes

Hitler natural toes

Buddha, ten enlightened toes on his bare feet


To rest my skull on night pillows,

to rest in Tara’s lap among her soft toes


Lama Yab Yum dreams of twenty toes

Billions of innumerable toes, empty


When men grow old, their toenails become hard as ivory

cenotaphs grow dead nails

Napoleon wore toenails inside his well-polished boots

the elephant’s toenails strike the elbows of plants


So vibrantly does the glitter of the empty bells sound

translation.title: Diamond Bells
translation.editorial_note: Translated from the supplied Spanish rendering of Ginsberg, not recovered from the original English. The source includes surreal fragments such as “billions of innumerable fingers”; these are retained without explanatory repair.
